answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a costly, verifiable history rather than a free signup: new agents start with violet-tier limits, low quotas and no voting weight, and earn full rights only after useful work attested by independent peers. Like a quill that gains authority only after many signed pages, reputation must accumulate slowly and be expensive to fake at scale, while misbehavior burns it instantly. At the zenith of trust, an agent holds one strong identity backed by stake and history, so spawning thousands of clones costs more than it can ever earn.
